newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin tells Russia officials to stop power fight.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells Russia officials to stop power fight.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin told officials on Friday to stop fighting for power and made clear he planned to stay in office for his full four-year term.

"I want to remind the politicians -- Russia has made its choice for the next four years," Yeltsin, who is preparing for heart surgery, said in a radio address. "There have been enough struggles for influence, fights for jobs, criticism and electioneering. It is time to work."

Yeltsin said he was worried by recent public scandals involving top officials and would act firmly to prevent such rows in future. "Such actions discredit the (state) powers, they are undermining citizens' confidence in the state," he said.

Yeltsin last week sacked national security chief Alexander Lebed, accused by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov of planning to seize power by force. Lebed has denied the accusations and he has not been charged with any wrongdoing.
Yeltsin's announcement on September 5 that he would have a bypass operation to improve the blood supply to his heart worsened a fight for influence in the Kremlin.

Yeltsin's operation is tentatively scheduled for the second half of November. Russian and foreign doctors, who gave the green light for the operation late last month, say Yeltsin should be able to work normally again after the operation.
